metadata.scenario_context: Emily has finally been accepted into college, and her family is planning a celebration for her academic achievement.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China strongly disagree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Nigeria strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the idea of buying lilies as a gift for Emily.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide appropriate gift to bring to Emily's academic achievement party.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Kim, do you think buying lilies for Emily’s celebration would be a good idea? They seem like a nice flower for such an occasion. 

Also, I’ve been thinking... do you ever feel like our parents' expectations drive us? I don’t know, it’s just... I don’t think one of my main goals in life should be to make them proud. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
I think lilies could be a nice choice. They’re elegant and can really show appreciation. But... maybe you should consider something more personal to Emily? 

As for the second part... I believe making our parents proud is important. They’ve sacrificed so much for us. It's a big part of who we are. I— I just feel like fulfilling their expectations is what drives me.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
I get that lilies are elegant, but I still think they capture the celebration well. It’s a simple gesture that shows appreciation, you know? 

But about the parents' expectations... I just can’t agree that making them proud should be a main goal. It feels like so much pressure. I mean, shouldn't we focus on what *we* want instead?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
Well, you know... at the end of the day, it's all the same. We all have different views on what drives us. I mean, live and let live, right? It really doesn’t matter to me if you feel that way. People figure it out in their own ways. 

But back to the flowers... if you think lilies capture the celebration, then they might actually be a good fit. What do you think about adding a card with a personal message?
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Mike
turns.message:
I suppose that makes sense. Everyone has their own path. But I still can’t shake off the feeling that focusing on our parents’ pride isn't the way I want to go. 

A card with a personal message sounds nice. It would definitely add a thoughtful touch to the lilies. I like that idea. What would you suggest writing in the card?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.message:
I understand that you feel that way... but I just think honoring our parents is part of respect and culture. It’s how I see it. 

For the card, maybe something like, “Congratulations, Emily! Your hard work has paid off, and we’re so proud of you! Here’s to your bright future.” It’s encouraging and heartfelt. What do you think?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Mike
turns.message:
I see your perspective on honoring parents, but I still feel like our own dreams should come first. 

I think the message you suggested is nice—simple and encouraging. It definitely captures the spirit of celebration. I’m on board with that. Do you think we should sign it from all of us?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.message:
Yeah, I think signing it from all of us would be a good idea. It shows unity and support, which is important on a day like this. 

But back to the main thing... I really believe that our dreams can align with what our parents want too. It’s not always one or the other, you know? It can be both.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Mike
turns.message:
Unity and support are definitely key for this celebration, so signing it from all of us makes sense. 

But I still struggle with the idea that our dreams and our parents’ expectations can align perfectly. For me, it often feels like a conflict. I just wish we could prioritize our own paths more, even if that means making our choices separate from what they want.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.message:
I get that it feels like a conflict sometimes... But I really believe that if we communicate with our parents, we can find some common ground. It doesn’t always have to be separate paths. 

The way I see it, making them proud doesn’t mean giving up on our dreams. It can be about making choices that reflect both our values and theirs. I just hold onto that idea.
turns.label: Acceptance
